name: Slack Tide

stars.name: Slack Tide A
stars.notes: A long-lived orange dwarf whose calm, amber light anchors the system; its steady output is the reason the tideworld below has never known a bad season.

stars.name: Slack Tide B
stars.notes: A dim red companion circling 40 AU out, close enough to paint auroras across the outer moons and far enough to leave the circumbinary orbits serene.

planets.name: Ebbstone
planets.notes: A scorched inner rock stripped of volatiles long ago; its daylit face glows dull red on approach, warning pilots off the innermost lane.

planets.name: Highwater
planets.notes: A warm circumbinary ocean world with no continents at all, only an endless sea broken by reef-archipelagos and the floating harbor-cities of forty million Tidewarden citizens.

planets.name: Drowned Court
planets.notes: A marginal world with thin air and shallow seas covering drowned ruins of a failed first colony; salvage crews are licensed to visit but never to stay overnight.

planets.name: Cauldron Swell
planets.notes: The system's great storm giant, banded ochre like old brass; its largest moon hosts the helium skimming works that fuel the Compact's patrol fleet.

planets.name: Fathom Barrow
planets.notes: A deep teal hydrogen world ringed by shepherd moons; survey buoys drift its upper layers mapping wind currents for reasons no one files publicly.

planets.name: Whitewrack
planets.notes: A fractured ice shell over a buried brine layer, glowing faintly under the companion's auroral lash; probe teams drill its cracks every few years.

planets.name: Low Anchor
planets.notes: The outermost sentinel, a dark frozen wanderer used as a navigation benchmark; its beacon is the last light outbound ships see.

anomalies.name: The Neap Echo
anomalies.notes: A faint temporal eddy where radio transmissions from hours past replay in sequence; navigators use it to verify their own logs, and the Tidewardens use it to watch for smugglers who haven't arrived yet.

asteroid_belts.name: Drift Net
asteroid_belts.notes: A broad belt of rock and ice harvested by licensed dredgers; the Compact stations customs pickets along its inner edge to catch unregistered traffic.

stations.name: Highwater Ring
stations.notes: The great tidal port above Highwater's seas, where ocean freighters, kelp barges, and liner packets moor in rotating shifts beneath the Compact's ensign.

stations.name: Slack Channel Station
stations.notes: A customs and rescue station buried in the belt; its cutters escort honest traffic through the lanes and drag wrecks out of them.

faction_control.notes: The Compact governs from Highwater Ring with a merchant-admiral council; dissent is managed through harbor fees rather than force, and so far that has sufficed.

history: Compact colonists fleeing the coreward charter wars seeded Highwater's seas three centuries ago and built their first harbor-city on the hull of the colony ship itself.
The Drowned Court colony failed within a generation when its atmosphere processors stalled; the Compact sealed the records, and what lies under those shallow seas is now a licensed secret.
Last year the Neap Echo began replaying transmissions that have not yet been sent, and the Compact has quietly moved a naval picket to the belt's far side.
description: Two stars share this sky: a steady amber primary and a small red companion wheeling far out like a lantern tied to a mooring line. Between them run seven quiet orbits, and around both circles Highwater, an ocean world without a single acre of land, its warm global sea broken only by reef chains and the tower-clusters of floating cities. From approach distance, the system looks like calm water after wind, which is exactly how its people prefer to be seen.

The Tidewarden Compact runs Slack Tide as a well-regulated port of call, taxing kelp harvests, helium skimmed from Cauldron Swell, and the steady liner traffic that crosses the Brineward Expanse. Forty million people live on and beneath Highwater's waves, and another forty-six thousand work Highwater Ring, where freighters queue in disciplined rotation. Traffic here is moderate, orderly, and watched; every ship that passes the Drift Net is logged twice, once by customs and once by the Neap Echo.

Beneath the calm, the water holds its questions. The ruins on Drowned Court predate any recorded wreck and show stonework no human colony shipped; Whitewrack's buried brine layer returned a single anomalous sensor pulse two years ago and nothing since. And the Echo has begun replaying voices that sound uncomfortably like the Compact's own admirals. The tide in this system is slack, but slack water, sailors know, never lasts.
